Here is a detailed numbered checklist of 100 practical steps for maintaining a software release archive, based on standard software engineering best practices and archival integrity principles.

1. Define a clear retention policy that specifies how long each type of software release must be kept.
2. Assign a unique, immutable identifier to every software release to prevent confusion between versions.
3. Store the source code for every release in a version control system with proper tagging.
4. Archive the compiled binaries or executable files associated with each specific release.
5. Preserve the build scripts and configuration files used to generate the release artifacts.
6. Save the dependency lock files to ensure the exact library versions can be reconstructed.
7. Archive the database schema migrations and scripts required for the release.
8. Store the environment configuration templates (e.g., .env.example) for each release.
9. Preserve the container images (Dockerfiles and built images) associated with the release.
10. Archive the infrastructure-as-code definitions (e.g., Terraform, CloudFormation) used for deployment.
11. Save the release notes and changelog documents for every version.
12. Archive the test reports and coverage metrics generated during the release process.
13. Preserve the security scan results and vulnerability assessments for each release.
14. Store the license files and third-party attribution notices for all included libraries.
15. Archive the API documentation and interface specifications for the release.
16. Save the user manuals and end-user documentation associated with the software.
17. Preserve the installation guides and deployment instructions for the release.
18. Archive the checksums (e.g., SHA-256) for all release artifacts to verify integrity.
19. Store digital signatures for all binaries and packages to ensure authenticity.
20. Preserve the public keys used to verify the digital signatures of the releases.
21. Archive the build logs to provide a traceable history of the compilation process.
22. Save the CI/CD pipeline configuration files used to automate the release.
23. Preserve the artifact repository metadata (e.g., Nexus, Artifactory) for each release.
24. Archive the issue tracker links and commit messages associated with the release.
25. Store the code review records and approval logs for the release branch.
26. Preserve the performance benchmark results for the release version.
27. Archive the compatibility matrix showing supported
